findings: All 85 previously unattempted, currently unheld Stack-Edu records lack dataset commit IDs. The bounded recovery route requests up to five commits for the recorded path, then requires exact consumed bytes and Git blob identity at a recovered immutable revision. A matching revision does not reconstruct the dataset acquisition snapshot or prove the earliest source.

Ten new host origins, all C++, match retained SHA256 and plain SHA1 identities and Git blobs in complete trees. Ten ancestor notices are recovered and blob-verified. Notice availability does not decide applicability or training permission.

All 75 remain unresolved for infrastructure reasons; do not classify them as missing repositories, unsuitable content or failed byte matches.

The ten successes precede quota exhaustion in the fixed request order, so their language mix and recovery fraction do not support a source-quality or whole-stock recoverability estimate. Cached evidence preserves every response, including all 75 quota responses. A stop for fresh API requests after observed quota exhaustion was added after acquisition and checked offline; it did not prevent the already-recorded responses.
